play.definition: A post-snap option concept that combines a called run with one or more attached quick-pass routes. The quarterback receives the snap, establishes a mesh with the running back, reads a designated conflict defender, and either completes the handoff or pulls the ball and throws immediately to an attached receiver. The offensive line executes the called run-blocking scheme on both branches while the run and pass elements develop simultaneously.

action.label: Ball Snap
action.definition: The action of the center (or occasionally another player) legally putting the ball into play by handing or tossing it between their legs to a backfield player (typically the quarterback) to initiate a down.

action.label: None
action.definition: A temporal label used when the player is visible but is not performing any defined football action in the action taxonomy during the annotated interval.

action.label: Pre Snap
action.definition: The period before the snap when players are set in formation and no active play has begun.

action.label: Run After Catch
action.definition: A receiver's action of advancing the football after completing a catch, using acceleration, cuts, and open-field movement to gain additional yardage.

action.label: Secure Catch
action.definition: A receiver's action of establishing clear possession and control of a forward, lateral, or backward pass after the football reaches the hands or body.

action.label: Snap Receive
action.definition: The action of the quarterback securing the ball from the center’s snap to initiate the play.

action.label: Throw Screen Pass
action.definition: A quarterback's or other passer's action of delivering a short forward or lateral pass to an eligible receiver positioned near or behind blockers for a designed screen play.

action.label: Turn To Quarterback
action.definition: A receiver's action of rotating the head, shoulders, hips, or entire body toward the quarterback to locate the ball and present a receiving target.
